transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-02 15:00 PT | 75 mins | BlueCliff Telemetry POC workshop
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Noah (Redwood SE), Maya (BlueCliff Head of ML), Omar (BlueCliff Platform), Sarah (BlueCliff Privacy), Derek (Product), Rajiv (CTO, joined late)
Link references: Redwood bench template https://redwood.ai/poc/bench-template | Security summary https://redwood.ai/security/soc2-summary.pdf

--- Auto Summary (may be imperfect) ---
Jordan: quick overview of what we'll cover, timeline 2-4 weeks pilot, success criteria.
Maya: primary goal is reliability of summaries for telemetry events, hallucination tolerance ~very low.

--- Action items (auto) ---
See action_items field sent separately.

00:00:08 Jordan (Redwood): ok hey everyone thanks for joining um we'll run through the eval plan and then map that to a bench timeline, I'm Jordan AE at Redwood, Priya and Noah from the SE team here.
00:00:22 Maya (BlueCliff): hey thanks, excited, we want to measure not just accuracy but also strict JSON conformance because our pipeline ingests the output.
00:00:35 Priya (Redwood SE): quick question on ingestion format — is it a fixed schema or flexible key-values?
00:00:42 Omar (BlueCliff): it's fixed, we have an event-summary schema with required fields: event_type, severity, timestamp_iso, summary_text, device_id, tags. If summary_text is malformed or hallucinated it's a big problem.
00:00:58 Priya: understood — so format checks will be first-class. we'll run schema validation and count failures.
00:01:10 Jordan: high-level POC: phase 1 is quality eval (golden prompts + regression), phase 2 is load and latency benchmarks and then a short pilot on dedicated if needed.
00:01:22 Derek: timeline? we want a decision in ~4 weeks.
00:01:27 Jordan: yes 3-4 weeks is doable if datasets are ready quickly.
00:02:05 Priya: about golden prompts — recommend 3 buckets: core, edge, adversarial. core are frequent telemetry queries, edge are long-context or low-signal cases, adversarial are prompts that historically produce hallucinations or format errors. aim for 400-600 golden prompts to start.
00:02:29 Maya: we can do 500, and we'll flag 50 of those with ground truth for hallucination check.
00:02:40 Noah: for regression tests, we suggest a larger corpus 2-5k cases that include historical failures plus synthetic variations (timezones, device ID formats, noisy logs). We'll run daily regression during pilot.
00:03:12 Sarah (Privacy): what about PII? our telemetry sometimes includes device owner PII, we need to confirm redaction, retention and whether tokens are stored.
00:03:24 Jordan: good point. Redwood hosted keeps minimal logs by default for pilot and we can enable customer-managed KMS for private deployment. We'll send the security pack.
00:03:37 Omar: also looking at data residency — some customers must keep data in EU region, we might require dedicated in-region nodes.
00:03:46 Priya: noted — regional routing can be part of test plan when we do dedicated runs.
00:04:05 Maya: ok can we define pass/fail thresholds now?
00:04:10 Jordan: yes here's a starting recommendation: format compliance >= 98% (JSON schema), hallucination rate <= 2% on labelled set, semantic similarity (embedding-based) >= 0.85 avg on summaries against ground truth, manual review sample AUC > 90% acceptance. Latency targets: p95 < 250ms for short prompts (<= 128 tokens), p99 < 500ms. Cost targets we can discuss but core is quality first.
00:04:41 Derek: curious about how hallucination rate is measured — what counts?
00:04:46 Priya: we'll use a labeled ground-truth set (50-100 items) and automated heuristics: presence of invented device IDs, contradicting timestamps, or made-up facts compared to the ingested log. We'll have human adjudication on borderline cases.
00:05:05 Noah: also add factuality checks using external lookups where possible (e.g., device registry) — we can automate some of that.
00:05:17 Maya: that sounds good. are we using fidelity metrics like BLEU or ROUGE?
00:05:23 Priya: those are ok but brittle. we prefer a mixed scoring: (1) schema pass/fail (binary), (2) exact/partial match on critical keys, (3) embedding similarity on narrative fields (cosine sim), (4) manual rating for ambiguous cases. we'll weight schema 40%, factuality 30%, semantic similarity 20%, manual 10%.
00:05:52 Jordan: example scoring: 0.98 schema pass -> 0.98*0.4 = 0.392, factuality 0.95->0.285, semantic 0.86->0.172, manual 0.9->0.09 => total ~0.939, pass if >0.9.
00:06:15 Maya: ok that weighted approach is helpful.
00:06:30 Priya: on hallucination tests specifically, we'll create negative controls (prompts with missing fields) and known-trap prompts. We'll compute false positive hallucination rate and false negative.
00:06:44 Omar: for load — our production peaks ~120 RPS with spikes to 250 for a few minutes. we'd like to see how caching and batching affect token cost and latency.
00:06:57 Noah: we'll simulate 3 traffic profiles: steady 50 RPS (baseline), production spike 120-250 RPS, and burst 400 RPS for resilience checks. Redwood recommends testing with prefix/KV caching toggled on and off.
00:07:19 Priya: we'll provide an autoscaling config suggestion for Dedicated runs — min nodes, burst pool etc — but for the pilot we'll run both hosted (Redwood-managed) and dedicated (reserved) to compare latency/cost.
00:07:36 Maya: any suggestions on prompt engineering? we want deterministic JSON output, sometimes the model puts brackets or stray commas.
00:07:44 Priya: include a strict output instruction block, provide schema in the system prompt and a few examples (few-shot). Also include a validator step: if output fails schema, re-prompt with "fix format only" up to 2 times, then mark as failure. We'll measure improvement from repair flow.
00:08:08 Jordan: note that repair attempts increase tokens/cost and add latency; we'll trade off by measuring success per dollar for each policy.
00:08:20 Derek: how do we do regression tests across model versions? we have to detect quality regressions when Redwood swaps a kernel or model variant.
00:08:28 Priya: Redwood Optimize can run nightly regression comparing current model to baseline using the regression suite. We'll produce a regression report and alert on >2% drop in weighted score. We can also pin customers to a model version during rollout.
00:08:45 Maya: fine. what about hallucination types — short hallucinations (made-up device name) vs long (invented causal chains)?
00:08:53 Noah: we'll tag examples by hallucination class and run per-class thresholds. For critical fields (device_id, timestamp_iso) tolerance is zero. For narrative summary_text we allow some paraphrase but check for invented claims.
00:09:06 Sarah: any plan for human review load? we can't manually review thousands.
00:09:11 Priya: sample-based review: random 1% sample plus triggered review for schema failures and low-similarity cases. Also we'll prioritize human review for high-severity events.
00:09:30 Jordan: ok timeline recap: Week 0 (this week) gather seeds and golden prompts; Week 1 prepare harness + run small smoke tests; Week 2 run full quality eval (hosted + model variants); Week 3 load/latency benchmarks and decision. total ~3 weeks if datasets are ready.
00:09:52 Maya: works for us, we'll aim to deliver the seed dataset by next Friday.
00:10:08 Rajiv (joins late): apologies for delay — quick question on security — will logs include raw telemetry or only token-level metadata?
00:10:17 Jordan: for hosted pilot we do transient token logs for troubleshooting; for enterprise/private we support no-logs and KMS. we'll send the security pack.
00:10:30 Derek: pricing expectation — do you have a pilot discount or trial credits?
00:10:35 Jordan: yes we typically offer pilot credits for first 100k tokens and a pilot rate card for dedicated sizing; I'll follow up in email with numbers.
00:10:50 Maya: ok let's talk specifics of golden prompt design — examples should include multi-turn context where the model must maintain state across messages — like a device reported error then follow-up clarifies severity.
00:11:05 Priya: include both single-shot and multi-turn cases; for multi-turn include KV cache behavior to simulate long lived chat contexts. We'll test different max context lengths.
00:11:23 Noah: technical deep-dive note: we'll also test quantized model variants vs full precision on dedicated to measure latency/cost tradeoffs and any quality delta.
00:11:36 Omar: can we have offline scoring script? we prefer to run analysis in our infra.
00:11:41 Noah: yes we'll provide a scoring harness (python) that runs locally against exported responses; includes schema validator, embedding sim, and summary scorer. We'll share on repo link.
00:11:55 Priya: we'll also include a small UI in Redwood Console to inspect flagged failures and trace token-level costs per call.
00:12:05 Jordan: next steps again: share golden prompt template, security docs, pilot contract, bench harness, and confirm dataset delivery date.
00:12:18 Maya: agreed. thanks everyone.

(Transcript continues with Q&A and some cross talk; below are snippets to capture authenticity)
00:25:02 Jordan: uh — just to call out, when we say hallucination <=2% that is measured on the labeled set, we will also publish a confidence interval around that because sample sizes matter.
00:35:20 Omar: we have some proprietary device registry we can expose for lookups in the late stages of the pilot, not in week 1.
00:42:00 Priya: note, for format repair loop, we'll log both original and repaired outputs to evaluate repair efficacy. sometimes repair can mask deeper model failures so we'll keep both.
00:50:15 Derek: any blockers? Sarah: need to review data-flow with legal for PII before we share raw logs — that might push dataset delivery by a few days.
00:58:30 Jordan: that's fine — we can run synthetic examples in meantime.
01:12:00 (approx) Meeting end: recap of action items and ownership, agree to follow up email.
